title: 2022 AMC 10A Problem 4
statement: In some countries, automobile fuel efficiency is measured in liters per \(100\) kilometers while other countries use miles per gallon. Suppose that \(1\) kilometer equals \(m\) miles, and \(1\) gallon equals \(l\) liters. Which of the following gives the fuel efficiency in liters per \(100\) kilometers for a car that gets \(x\) miles per gallon?

solutions.text:
A car that gets \(x\) miles per gallon uses \(\frac{1}{x}\) gallons per mile.

Since \(1\) mile is \(\frac{1}{m}\) kilometers, this is \(\frac{m}{x}\) gallons per kilometer.

Multiplying by \(l\) liters per gallon gives \(\frac{lm}{x}\) liters per kilometer, so for \(100\) kilometers the fuel used is \(\frac{100lm}{x}\) liters.

Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: Convert miles per gallon into gallons per kilometer first
Liters per \(100\) kilometers is the reciprocal style of miles per gallon
